headline: Uprising over the collapsing rial meets a massacre
text: Protests that began on 28 December as the rial fell to record lows, near 1.5 million to the dollar, and food prices soared, spread to hundreds of towns in every province. On 8 and 9 January, as huge crowds filled the streets, the authorities shut down the internet and security forces opened fire. Rights groups say thousands of people were killed in those two days, and tens of thousands arrested; the government gives lower figures, and with the internet cut the numbers cannot be checked.
imageCaption: Demonstrators with Iranian flags in support of the uprising in Iran, 10 January 2026

headline: Greg Abel takes over Berkshire
text: Greg Abel became Berkshire Hathaway's chief executive on 1 January, with Warren Buffett staying on as chairman. This month Berkshire completed the purchase of the chemicals maker OxyChem from Occidental Petroleum, announced last year.
imageCaption: Greg Abel and Warren Buffett walk through the exhibition hall of the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting, Omaha, 3 May 2025

headline: Merger talks with Rio Tinto
text: Glencore confirmed on 9 January that it is in preliminary talks with Rio Tinto about combining some or all of their businesses, possibly an all-share merger in which Rio would acquire Glencore. Rio has until 5 February to make a firm offer or walk away. Copper averaged a record $13,012 a tonne in January.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/statement-regarding-rio-tinto/9342767; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The high Andes near the Collahuasi copper mine, Chile

headline: Gold passes 5,000, then crashes on the new Fed chair
text: Gold rose above 5,000 dollars an ounce on 26 January and reached a record of about 5,600 on the 29th, as tensions over Venezuela, Iran and Greenland and fears for the Fed's independence drove buyers in. On 30 January the president named Kevin Warsh, seen as a defender of a strong dollar, as the next Fed chairman, and gold fell around 10 percent in a day while silver lost about 30 percent. Gold still averaged 4,753 dollars in January, 10 percent more than in December. The Fed has held its rate at 3.5 to 3.75 percent since December.
imageCaption: People queue outside a gold dealer in Hong Kong as gold passes 5,000 dollars an ounce, 28 January 2026
imageCredit: Photo by Peter PARKS / AFP via Getty Images

headline: Strong results, falling shares: fears about AI and spending
text: On 28 January Microsoft reported revenue of 81.3 billion dollars for the quarter to December, up 17%, with Azure up 39% and cloud revenue above 50 billion dollars. But the shares are falling: investors worry that software written by AI could replace much of what existing business software does, and that Microsoft is spending hundreds of billions on AI data centres, pushing its free cash flow down.
imageCaption: Satya Nadella at a White House dinner for technology leaders, September 2025

headline: Maduro captured, Iran in turmoil
text: US forces captured Venezuela's president Nicolas Maduro on 3 January, after a US blockade of sanctioned Venezuelan tankers since December. In Iran, security forces violently suppressed mass protests, and the US is building up forces in the region. US crude rose 13% in January to $64.50, from about $56 early in the month.
imageCaption: Nicolas Maduro aboard the USS Iwo Jima after his capture, January 2026

headline: BYD overtakes Tesla, and the Model S and X are dropped
text: Full-year figures published on 2 January showed that China's BYD sold more electric cars than Tesla in 2025 (2.26 million against 1.64 million), ending Tesla's run as the largest maker. On 28 January Musk said Tesla will stop making the Model S and Model X in the second quarter and use the Fremont space to build its Optimus humanoid robot.
imageCaption: The BYD Seal electric sedan

headline: Venezuela, dearer oil and record output lift ExxonMobil
text: After US forces captured Venezuela's president Maduro on 3 January, President Trump met oil executives on 9 January and said they would invest 100 billion dollars there; ExxonMobil's Darren Woods called Venezuela 'uninvestable' under current law, and Trump said he was inclined to keep ExxonMobil out. Oil rose anyway: US crude went from about 57 to 65 dollars during the month as unrest in Iran threatened supply. On 30 January ExxonMobil reported 2025 earnings of 28.8 billion dollars, its highest oil and gas output in more than 40 years and 37.2 billion returned to shareholders.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_intervention_in_Venezuela (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_of_oil (January 2026 Iran supply worries) (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 30 January 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408826000033/livef8k4q25991.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: An oil tanker crossing Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela

headline: Josh D'Amaro named Disney's next chief executive
text: On 3 February Disney's board unanimously chose Josh D'Amaro, head of the parks and experiences business, to succeed Bob Iger as chief executive from 18 March. Dana Walden becomes president and chief creative officer.
imageCaption: Josh D'Amaro, chairman of Disney's parks, speaks at the D23 Brazil fan event, São Paulo, November 2024

headline: An AI coding tool sends IBM to its worst day in 25 years
text: On 23 February the AI company Anthropic said its Claude Code tool can cut the time to modernise programs written in COBOL, the old language that runs on IBM mainframes, from years to quarters for some projects. IBM shares fell about 13% that day, their steepest daily fall since October 2000, and the drop spread to IT service firms.
imageCaption: Arvind Krishna, IBM's chief executive

headline: US and Israel go to war with Iran; Khamenei is killed
text: On 28 February, after weeks of the biggest US military build-up in the region since 2003 and while nuclear talks were still under way, American missiles and drones and Israeli jets struck targets across Iran. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in Tehran along with several senior officials. Hundreds of Iranians have been killed or injured, the Red Crescent reports damage in 24 provinces, and the internet is almost entirely cut. The Revolutionary Guards have warned ships that none may pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
imageCaption: An Israeli F-35 fighter jet during the 'Roaring Lion' operation against Iran

headline: Navratil's plan: 16,000 jobs, water out, more growth
text: On 19 February Nestlé reported 2025 organic growth of 3.5% with positive volume growth in every zone and expects around 3% to 4% for 2026. It plans to cut about 16,000 jobs by the end of 2027, raised its savings target, is negotiating to sell its remaining ice cream business to Froneri and has started a process for its waters business.
imageCaption: Philipp Navratil, chief executive of Nestlé, early 2026

headline: John Furner takes over a trillion-dollar Walmart
text: John Furner became Walmart's president and chief executive on 1 February. In February Walmart became the first traditional retailer to be valued at more than one trillion dollars. It employs about 2.1 million people, more than any other private company.
imageCaption: John Furner (left), Walmart's incoming chief executive, with Doug McMillon

headline: Rio walks away; a US-backed buyer for Congo
text: On 5 February Rio Tinto said it would not make an offer; Glencore said Rio wanted both the chairman and chief executive roles and an ownership split that undervalued Glencore's copper business. On 3 February Glencore had agreed in principle to sell 40% of its Congo copper and cobalt mines, Kamoto and Mutanda, to the US-backed Orion Critical Mineral Consortium at an enterprise value of about $9bn. Its 2025 results showed adjusted EBITDA of $13.5bn and net debt of $11.2bn.
imageCaption: The Mutanda copper and cobalt mine, Democratic Republic of the Congo

headline: Fourth-quarter results and a strong month for the share
text: Novartis reported on 4 February that fourth-quarter sales rose 1% in dollars (down 1% at constant currencies) to $13.3 billion, with net income down 15%. The share rose strongly in February and reached a record.
imageCaption: The entrance to the Novartis campus, Basel

headline: Hormuz closed, oil above 100 dollars, a new Supreme Leader
text: Iran has fired missiles and drones at Israel, US bases and Gulf states, and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell by about 70 percent; some 2,000 ships are stranded in the Gulf. Brent crude passed 100 dollars a barrel on 8 March for the first time in four years. On 8 March the Assembly of Experts named Khamenei's son Mojtaba as Supreme Leader. Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah has resumed and Israeli troops have entered southern Lebanon. Stock markets fell, hardest in Asia, where South Korea's index lost up to 12 percent in a day.
imageCaption: Petrol prices jump at a filling station during the Iran war, March 2026

headline: War with Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz
text: The US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, through which about a quarter of the world's seaborne oil passes; Gulf output fell by at least 10 million barrels a day and Qatar halted gas exports. Brent passed $100 on 8 March and ended March near $120 on futures markets, the largest monthly rise ever. The US is releasing 172 million barrels from its reserve.
imageCaption: Smoke on the shore seen from a vessel stranded in the Strait of Hormuz as ship traffic all but stops, 5 March 2026
imageCredit: Photo by Stringer/Anadolu via Getty Images

headline: War with Iran closes Hormuz and oil passes 100 dollars
text: US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on 28 February. Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, the route for much of the world's oil, and on 9 March Brent crude touched 119.50 dollars, up 29 percent in a day, before settling around 100. US crude averaged about 91 dollars in March, against 65 in February. ExxonMobil, with big production in the Americas, gains from the higher price, though some of its Middle East output is disrupted.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_of_oil (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 1 May 2026 (Middle East volume impacts), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408826000065/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Strait of Hormuz seen from space

headline: War with Iran and AI fears: shares fall 5 percent
text: The S&P 500 set a record of 7,002.28 on 28 January, but software companies fell on fears that artificial intelligence would disrupt their business. Then American and Israeli strikes on Iran began on 28 February, oil futures rose about 50% and the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed, raising fears of inflation. The S&P 500 lost 5% in March to 6,528.52, its worst month in a year.
imageCaption: Protest against the war with Iran, Bristol, 21 March 2026

headline: War with Iran hits European car makers
text: The United States and Israel went to war with Iran on 28 February. Iran attacked shipping and blocked the Strait of Hormuz, energy prices jumped and stock markets fell. The Middle East is a high-margin market for luxury cars, and higher energy prices weigh on Europe's economy.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war (read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Iran war poses challenges to high-margin Middle East car market', 18 March 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Strait of Hormuz seen from space

headline: The Iran war hits Europe's industry
text: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 February, Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz on 4 March. Brent crude passed 120 dollars, European gas prices nearly doubled, and the European Central Bank postponed rate cuts and warned of stagflation. Siemens shares fell 19% in March.
imageCaption: Countries struck by the United States, Israel or Iran, as of 14 March 2026

headline: War in the Gulf: SLB pulls crews out of the Middle East
text: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on 28 February and Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, SLB said on 11 March that it had suspended travel in the region and begun to demobilise operations in a few countries as customers protect staff and facilities. First-quarter revenue will be lower than expected, costing about 6 to 9 cents a share. Oil has passed 100 dollars.
source: SLB press release of 11 March 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312526101131/d17166dex99.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_of_oil (read 2026-10-03); SLB press release of 24 April 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312526174940/d111579dex99.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Strait of Hormuz seen from space

headline: Sony hands its TV business to a venture led by TCL
text: Sony and the Chinese electronics maker TCL agreed to form a joint venture for televisions, professional displays and home audio. TCL holds 51% and runs development, manufacturing and distribution; Sony keeps 49% and licenses the brand and core technology.
imageCaption: A Sony Bravia television on display at CES, Las Vegas, January 2011

headline: Intel more than doubles in a month
text: On 9 April Intel's foundry won Tesla as a long-term partner for a planned chip plant and Alphabet committed to Intel processors for Google Cloud. On 23 April Intel reported first-quarter revenue of 13.6 billion dollars, up 7%, and adjusted earnings of 29 cents a share against two cents expected; chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said demand for data-centre processors now exceeds supply. The shares rose 24% the next day and 114% for the month.
imageCaption: Intel's factory campus at Leixlip, Ireland

headline: Tim Cook will hand over to John Ternus
text: On 20 April Apple announced that Tim Cook will become executive chair on 1 September and that John Ternus, 50, head of hardware engineering and at Apple since 2001, will succeed him as chief executive. On 30 April Apple reported record March-quarter revenue of 111.2 billion dollars, up 17%, with strong demand for the iPhone 17.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000114036126015711/ef20071035_8k.htm (Apple 8-K of 20 April 2026, read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000011/a8-kex991q2202603282026.htm (Apple press release of 30 April 2026, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: John Ternus, Apple's head of hardware engineering, at Apple's 50th anniversary event, March 2026

headline: Ceasefire and strong earnings: the best month since 2020
text: President Trump announced a two-week ceasefire with Iran late on 7 April; the next day oil fell about 15% and the Dow jumped 1,326 points. The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,022.95 on 15 April, though the Strait of Hormuz stayed effectively closed, as 84% of companies beat profit forecasts and technology shares led on optimism about AI. The S&P 500 rose 10% in April to a record 7,209.01, its best month since November 2020.
imageCaption: Pentagon briefing on the ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran, 8 April 2026

headline: AI orders send Cisco to a record
text: Cisco reported on May 13 record quarterly sales of $15.8 billion, up 12%, with product orders up 35%. It now expects $9 billion of orders for AI infrastructure this fiscal year, up from $5 billion, and raised its full-year forecast. It also announced a restructuring with up to $1 billion of charges to shift spending to silicon, optics, security and AI.
imageCaption: The Cisco sign over the company's pavilion at the World Economic Forum in Davos

headline: Milan Nedeljković becomes BMW's chief executive
text: At the annual general meeting on 13 May, Oliver Zipse handed over the chairmanship of the board of management to Milan Nedeljković, until now the board member for production.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (list of chairmen, BMW Group press release of 13 May 2026, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Milan Nedeljković, BMW's production chief and its chief executive from May 2026, in BMW work wear

headline: eBay rejects a $56 billion bid from GameStop
text: On May 3 the video game retailer GameStop, which holds about 5% of eBay, proposed to buy eBay for about $56 billion in cash and shares. eBay rejected it as 'neither credible nor attractive'.
imageCaption: The sign in front of eBay's headquarters in San Jose, California

headline: Intel passes its 2000 peak on talk of an Apple deal
text: Bloomberg reported that Apple has held talks with Intel and Samsung about making its main device processors in the United States, which would reduce its dependence on TSMC. Intel's shares jumped 13% on 5 May and on 8 May traded above 130 dollars, far above their August 2000 record of 74.88 dollars.
source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/05/intel-intc-stock-apple-talks-report.html (read 2026-10-03, via search summary); https://www.ghacks.net/2026/05/08/intel-stock-hits-all-time-high-after-report-of-apple-chip-manufacturing-talks/ (read 2026-10-03, via search summary)
imageCaption: Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, California

headline: BMW warns of a 'significant' profit fall
text: On 16 June BMW cut its forecast for 2026: it now expects a significant fall in pre-tax profit and a car margin of only 1 to 3%, down from 4 to 6%, because the Chinese market is shrinking faster than expected under strong local competition and the war with Iran keeps energy costs high and weighs on demand. The shares fell to their lowest level since 2020.
source: Yahoo Finance, 'BMW warns of significant profit decline as shares fall 7%', 17 June 2026, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bmw-warns-significant-profit-decline-104414505.html (read 2026-10-03); Reuters, 'BMW shares sink after profit warning highlights China and Iran risk', 17 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); data/out/bmw.json (dividend in May 2026) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The BMW headquarters and plant at Munich seen from above

headline: Intel falls a third from its June high
text: Chip shares fell from 1 July after Bank of America warned that AI chip valuations had run ahead of demand. On 23 July Intel reported second-quarter revenue of 16.1 billion dollars, up 25%, and adjusted earnings of 42 cents, double the forecast, but raised its 2026 capital spending plan to more than 20 billion dollars; the shares closed 7.9% lower the next day. Reports also said its newest 18A process may not reach profitable yields until late 2026 or 2027.
imageCaption: Intel's headquarters on Mission College Boulevard, Santa Clara

headline: Ceasefire breaks down; millions mourn Khamenei
text: The truce collapsed on 8 July after Iran attacked commercial ships, insisting on its control of the Strait of Hormuz, and the US resumed strikes it says are meant to protect shipping. Iran accuses Washington of breaking 'nearly all parts' of the June agreement. From 3 to 9 July a state funeral for Ali Khamenei drew millions across Iran.
imageCaption: Mourners fill the Mosalla in Tehran for the state funeral of Ayatollah Khamenei, 5 July 2026

headline: Azure passes 100 billion dollars, and the shares recover
text: On 29 July Microsoft reported revenue of 90.0 billion dollars for the quarter to June, up 18%. Azure revenue passed 100 billion dollars for the year and Microsoft 365 Copilot has more than 30 million paid users; results included a 3.2 billion dollar gain on Microsoft's investment in Anthropic. The shares rose 25% in July.
imageCaption: Microsoft's campus in Redmond, Washington

headline: Korea's chip crash
text: South Korea's stock market crashed in July, the KOSPI index losing more than 40% in about 40 days as investors sold Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the memory-chip makers that make up more than half of it. The fear is that big technology companies, which have not yet earned back their AI spending, will order fewer high-bandwidth memory chips.
imageCaption: A DDR5 memory module from SK hynix, one of Korea's two big memory-chip makers

headline: Record deliveries, but profits disappoint
text: Tesla delivered a record 480,126 cars in the second quarter, but on 22 July it reported earnings of 33 cents a share against expected 53 cents; its operating margin fell to 1.4%, regulatory credit income collapsed and spending on factories and AI more than doubled, so it burned cash. The shares fell about 10% the next day. Musk's SpaceX listed its shares in June in the biggest stock market debut ever, competing for the same investors.
source: Tesla Q2 2026 Production and Deliveries, 2 July 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026046717/exhibit99111111.htm (read 2026-10-03); Electrek, 'Tesla (TSLA) releases Q2 2026 financial results: record revenue, big profit miss', 22 July 2026, https://electrek.co/2026/07/22/tesla-tsla-q2-2026-financial-results/ (read 2026-10-03); 24/7 Wall St., 'Tesla Slides 10% on Earnings Miss Despite Record Deliveries', 23 July 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); NPR, 'SpaceX IPO makes history as largest ever', 12 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/06/why-tesla-stock-plunged-26-in-july/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Tesla Model Y in a Tesla showroom

headline: Revenue doubles again: 96 billion dollars a quarter
text: On 26 August Nvidia reported revenue of 96.2 billion dollars for the quarter to July, up 106% from a year earlier, with data-centre revenue of 89.0 billion. Jensen Huang said AI has reached its inflection point and demand is accelerating; its Vera Rubin systems are in full production.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang with students at Stanford, 30 April 2026

headline: McDonald's 'NEXT' plan: billions in support for franchisees
text: On 23 September McDonald's presented its 'NEXT' strategy to win back customers in a sluggish US market. It plans about 8.5 billion dollars of support for franchisees through 2036, about 5 billion of it by 2030, in rent relief and capital, to modernise restaurants, and targets an operating margin in the low-to-mid 50% range by 2030. McDonald's shares fell about 12% in September; they have lost about a third since February.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000006390826000076/exhibit991-investorupdate2.htm (release of 23 September 2026, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald%27s (US sales, read 2026-10-03); price changes from data/out/mcd.json
imageCaption: Chris Kempczinski, McDonald's chief executive
imageCredit: Ambassador of the United States of America to the People's R

headline: The Fed raises rates again as oil passes 100 dollars
text: On 16 September the Fed raised its rate by a quarter point to 3.75 to 4 percent, unanimously, its first increase since July 2023; the Committee pointed to persistent pressure in energy and consumer prices, and most members expect another increase this year. Consumer prices in August were 3.4 percent higher than a year earlier, and oil passed 100 dollars a barrel in early September as the conflict with Iran escalated. The 10-year Treasury yield averaged about 5 percent in September, the highest since 2007, and a 30-year mortgage costs about 7 percent.
imageCaption: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the press conference after the Fed's rate rise, Washington, 16 September 2026

headline: John Ternus takes over
text: On 1 September John Ternus became Apple's chief executive, and Tim Cook executive chair.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000114036126035325/ef20081427_8ka.htm (Apple 8-K/A of 1 September 2026, read 2026-10-03, via EDGAR search listing); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Apple_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Tim Cook and John Ternus with Roberta Metsola, President of the European Parliament, May 2026

headline: BMW at a six-year low before its strategy day
text: BMW shares fell to their lowest since 2020 in September, down about 40% this year. At its capital markets day on 30 September the new chief executive Nedeljković promised a car margin of 3 to 5% by 2028 and 8 to 10% in the early 2030s, with a simpler model range, cheaper local parts and fewer dealers in China; about 8,000 jobs have already been cut. Some investors had hoped for more, but analysts called it the beginning of a healing process.
source: MarketScreener, 'BMW Investors' Nervousness Over Capital Markets Day Statements Eases', 30 September 2026, https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bmw-investors-nervousness-over-capital-markets-day-statements-eases-ce785ad2dd8ef024 (read 2026-10-03); Yahoo Finance Singapore, 'BMW plans margin rebuild with simpler line-up and pricier cars', https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/bmw-plans-margin-rebuild-simpler-041200536.html (read 2026-10-03); Investing.com, 'BMW stock hits a fresh 6-year low ahead of next week's CMD', 24 September 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The BMW iX3 of the Neue Klasse at the IAA Summit, Munich, September 2025

headline: AI agents lift Intel again
text: Intel's shares rose more than 40% in September. On 21 September they jumped 12% when reports said the success of Meta's Muse AI agent app could raise demand for processors; AMD rose 10% the same day. Intel had said in July that data-centre revenue grew 59% and that server chip demand exceeds supply.
imageCaption: Intel's chip factories in Chandler, Arizona

headline: Mercedes falls to a new low on China and Washington
text: Mercedes-Benz shares hit a 52-week low of about 40 euros on 30 September, down a third this year. Its sales in China collapsed by 30% in the second quarter. A US Senate bill against Chinese-owned car makers would have covered Mercedes, which is almost 20% owned by Chinese investors, until a senator said at the end of the month that Mercedes will be exempted. The company is buying back shares and plans a voluntary severance scheme.
source: AD HOC NEWS, 'Mercedes-Benz Dodges Washington's China Crosshairs as Buyback Engine Idles Toward October Test', 1 October 2026, https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/mercedes-benz-dodges-washington-s-china-crosshairs-as-buyback-engine-idles-toward-october-test/70210921 (read 2026-10-03); Carscoops, 'Mercedes Will Avoid US Ban, Despite 20% Chinese Ownership', https://www.carscoops.com/2026/10/mercedes-benz-avoids-chinese-car-ban-us/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Stuttgart with the Mercedes-Benz Untertürkheim plant
